entry_state: An acquired derivative's price is an asset origin,not a hedge gain. Instrument reductions preserve gains earned while designated and leave the hedged purchase unchanged;later undesignated changes enter profit. Matched purchase-portion cessation freezes a reserve whose release depends on expectation and loss recovery. Different designation prices defeat nominal-percentage allocation. The origin-matched derivation separates continuing reserve,frozen reserve and post-cessation gains;its terminal inventory bridge continues after page216. A false backward reference on213 is queued as RR346-007.
exit_state: Origin-matched cessation retains gross cash origins and tests liquidity before receipts. Purchase moves the hedge reserve into inventory basis without new income or cash. Later sales allocate carrying cost and allowance only to remaining goods;recovery cannot restore allowance on goods already sold. Equal final totals can conceal wrong interim statements. Net hedges preserve gross transactions and their earnings periods,including qualifying nil-net positions. The new IFRS2 award section separates service/non-market vesting from market conditions;its first subsection continues after222.

findings.observation: Cessation and inventory methods preserve signs and prior releases. The staged-sale calculation keeps gross cost and allowance separately,preventing recovery of sold goods' allowance. Final equality is explicitly distinguished from correct interim accounting.

The net-hedge example preserves gross statement lines and explains the cross-period reserve rather than treating it as another derivative asset. The following award example explicitly separates IFRS synthetic cases from Apple's US-GAAP treatment.
